page: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores clocked at up to 3.7 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes 945 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local temporary storage and does not include hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded CPU capability, with the instance scoring in the top 25 percent for Geekbench single-core (1992.0) and stress-ng single-core performance (3079.96). Multi-core benchmarks place solidly in the middle tier, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 11726.0, a PassMark CPU score of 26254.79, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 105.06 GB/sec. Application tests show dependable execution across static web serving at 20.75 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 22.34 million operations per second. However, large-block uncached memory read bandwidth falls into the lower quartile at 37.84 GB/sec, and CPU-only large language model inference scales down significantly under heavy parameters, achieving only 4.47 tokens per second on 70B prompt processing.

Balancing dedicated high-frequency compute, integrated NVMe SSD ephemeral storage, and standard memory density, the D16ads_v6 delivers solid performance efficiency without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU instances. The bundled high-speed NVMe storage provides rapid scratch space without relying solely on network-attached disks. This configuration is well aligned with workloads such as mid-sized relational and NoSQL databases, text processing pipelines, CI/CD compilation jobs, application backends, and general-purpose enterprise services.

Operating on Hyper-V with x86_64 architecture, it features AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction extensions without GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles show top-quartile single-core CPU throughput and text processing efficiency, paired with consistent mid-tier multi-threaded and database metrics, including 22.34 million Redis SET operations per second. Uncached memory read bandwidth is comparatively restricted under large block sizes, limiting heavy in-memory data streaming. With its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory proportion and fast local scratch space, the instance provides cost-effective throughput for relational databases, enterprise web applications, text analysis, and build systems requiring dedicated CPU cores.
